transcript:
Header: 2027-04-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Leah Kim (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Atlas), Evan Brooks (Security), Maya Santos (Platform)
Summary: Intro + POC success criteria, discuss private networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), regions and data residency, egress constraints and billing, define benchmark plan and timeline.

[00:00] Leah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — I'm Leah, AE at Redwood. Marcus is our SE. Priya, Evan, Maya, thanks for carving out the time.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks, Leah. We're focused on a POC to validate private networking and residency for PHI workloads, we want to scope connectivity and benchmarks.
[00:30] Marcus: Great. High level, we'll cover options: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoint services), cross-region considerations, and then sizing + benchmarks — latency, throughput, and a 72-hour soak you asked about.
[00:48] Evan: quick note — Atlas must ensure data never egresses to public internet and keys must be customer-managed (KMS/HSM). Also SOC2 and audit logs are prerequisites.
[01:10] Marcus: Understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS integrations and can run in your VPC or a customer-dedicated VPC with a private control plane. We'll map both network patterns.
[01:30] Maya: Clarify terminology — when you say "control plane" do you mean anything that calls home? we need a non-internet path for everything, inc telemetry.
[01:45] Leah: Good callout. For the strictest pattern we do a VPC-peer/Transit-GW plus PrivateLink endpoints so the control plane traffic stays over private connectivity — no public egress. We'll document designs.
[02:05] Priya: Regions: we need EU data residency for a subset of patients and US for others. Can you pin models to region and limit cross-region caching?
[02:22] Marcus: Yes. We can deploy model runtime in specific regions (e.g., eu-west-1, us-east-1) and lock routing policies so requests never leave region. There's a caveat around centralized observability — you can keep logs in-region or ship them to your S3 with agreed egress controls.
[02:40] Evan: is the observability plane separate? we need audit logs in our account.
[02:48] Marcus: We can optionally deliver logs to your S3 or CloudWatch in your account via a VPC endpoint so they never traverse public net.
[03:00] Leah: Ok let's move to connectivity options.
[03:05] Marcus: Option A: VPC peering / Transit Gateway — simple, low-latency, but peering is not transitive so for multiple regions you may need TGW. Option B: AWS PrivateLink — exposes a VPC endpoint service from Redwood into your VPC; more controlled, supports IAM and endpoint policies, and often preferred for security teams because it's explicit.
[03:30] Priya: Any differences on bandwidth/throughput and egress billing?
[03:37] Marcus: PrivateLink has per-Gb charges and interface endpoints; VPC peering via TGW will have data transfer charges too (depends on region). We will include estimated egress costs in sizing. For heavy throughput (e.g., continuous high QPS), TGW/VPC peering tends to be more cost-efficient.
[03:58] Evan: Also need to know about TLS termination and who manages certs.
[04:04] Marcus: TLS is end-to-end; certificates are customer-managed in the Private deployment. For hosted variants we support mutual TLS and customer certs with SNI.
[04:18] Maya: What about IP ranges / firewall changes? we can't open broad ranges.
[04:25] Leah: We provide a minimal set of IPs and recommend using security groups and endpoint policies. For PrivateLink you'll create ENIs in subnets — tighten by SGs. For TGW you'll add routes to route tables.
[04:40] Priya: Let's talk success criteria for the POC.
[04:45] Marcus: Common success criteria we recommend: 1) Functional: model responses match the quality baseline for the chosen prompts, 2) Performance: 95th percentile latency under X ms (we typically use 95th < 800ms for chat at target prompt length), 3) Throughput: sustain Y QPS/concurrency with acceptable cost, 4) Security: no traffic to public internet and keys remain under your control, 5) Ops: logs and metrics delivered to your accounts and SSO/SAML integration works.
[05:14] Priya: Can you put numbers on X and Y? our target is about 200 concurrent chat sessions during peak, typical prompt ~150 tokens.
[05:26] Marcus: For 150-token prompts and 200 concurrent sessions, we're looking at ~30-40 reqs/s depending on user think times. For safety let's size for 100 RPS sustained with headroom. Latency target: median < 300ms per token, 95th < 900ms. We'll provide GPU hour estimates.
[05:45] Leah: We'll produce a workload sizing doc and recommended infra profile (GPUs, instance type, scaling policies).
[05:51] Evan: Benchmarks — how will they run? replay of production logs or synthetic?
[05:56] Marcus: Two-phase: 1) synthetic spike tests (load generator inside your VPC), 2) replay a scrubbed traffic trace if you can provide one. We'll run a 72-hour soak at target concurrency to validate autoscaling and KV cache behavior. We'll collect token-level latency, tail latencies, GPU utilization, and cost estimates.
[06:20] Maya: Is the load generator in our account?
[06:23] Marcus: Preferable — we'll provide an easy Terraform and Docker script you run in your dev VPC so traffic stays internal. If not possible we can provide a partner VPC approach via PrivateLink.
[06:35] Priya: Data residency again — if a user in EU hits a model deployed in US by mistake what happens?
[06:42] Marcus: We can enforce routing rules so requests are routed by region and fail closed if no local capacity. There's also an option to route to a smaller local model instead of crossing regions.
[06:58] Evan: Compliance questions — SOC2, penetration test reports, encryption at rest/intransit, KMS HSM availability.
[07:05] Leah: We'll attach SOC2 report; Redwood Private supports bring-your-own-KMS and HSM for key isolation. Pen test summary can be provided.
[07:15] Priya: Ok good. Timeline — what do you propose for the POC?
[07:20] Marcus: Proposed: Week 0 (this week) — finalize scope and connectivity choice; Week 1 — environment setup and network handshake (IAM roles, peering/privateLink, S3 endpoints); Week 2 — deploy runtime and run initial functional smoke tests; Week 3 — run synthetic benchmarks; Week 4 — 72-hour soak and produce report. So about 4 weeks end-to-end.
[07:47] Priya: Procurement windows may add time; our legal needs to review data processing addendum.
[07:52] Leah: We'll send standard DPA and then negotiate any special clauses.
[07:56] Maya: A few technical clarifications — do you support cross-account IAM roles to push logs to our account?
[08:02] Marcus: Yes; we can assume a role to write to your S3 or use your Kinesis/CloudWatch via endpoints.
[08:10] Evan: Are we comfortable with persistent KV caches in-memory holding transient PHI? Need to ensure memory is zeroed on termination.
[08:18] Marcus: Good point — our runtime supports TTL/eviction and we can run with no persistent disk for sensitive workloads; memory scrub options are documented and we can enforce process restart as part of scaling.
[08:35] Priya: On a PIN-level, we'd like a canonical checklist for network changes and an internal runbook for our infra team.
[08:43] Leah: We'll include a network checklist (subnets, SGs, routes, endpoints), a runbook for the benchmark and post-POC handoff.
[08:52] Marcus: For benchmarking metrics we'll deliver a spreadsheet with token counts, GPU hours, cost per 1M tokens, p95/p99 latencies, and recommendations for quantization/batching to reduce cost.
[09:06] Priya: Any red flags we should look out for?
[09:09] Marcus: Biggest risks: mismatch in traffic shaping (your dev dataset vs production), unexpected egress (logs or 3rd-party model calls), and scaling configs that cause cold starts. We'll mitigate with warm pools and KV caching.
[09:26] Leah: Pricing model for Private deployment will be a combination of reserved capacity + usage for bursts; we'll outline expected monthly committed spend based on sizing.
[09:36] Evan: Network ops question: what subnet ranges do you need? we don't want to open to entire VPC.
[09:42] Marcus: For PrivateLink we create ENIs in specific private subnets — you'll provide 2 private subnets per AZ and SGs. For peering/TGW we ask for specific route table entries. We'll include exact CIDR ranges in the checklist.
[09:58] Maya: Ok. For the benchmark run we need a list of metrics to export to our Prometheus/CloudWatch.
[10:05] Marcus: We'll export token-level metrics, request latencies, model cache hit rates, GPU util, error rates, and quota metrics. We'll give exporters or CloudWatch agent configs.
[10:20] Priya: Procurement will want clear exit criteria and acceptance tests.
[10:24] Leah: We'll write an acceptance doc: must pass functional tests, p95 latency targets, soak stability, and security checklist.
[10:34] Priya: That sounds good. Any blockers on Redwood's side?
[10:38] Marcus: Just need network contacts and permissions to set up endpoints/peering and a test dataset (scrubbed) or trace.
[10:47] Priya: I'll have Evan send the compliance matrix and Maya will coordinate the infra people.
[10:53] Evan: we'll try to get a scrubbed 48-hour trace and a sample set of prompts.
[10:58] Leah: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[11:02] Leah: Action items: Marcus will size GPU and provide cost estimate; Leah will send SOC2 and DPA and the network checklist; Priya/Evan will share traffic profile and confirm timeline. We'll target the benchmark run next Wednesday (2027-04-14) pending network setup.
[11:24] Priya: Works for me.
[11:27] Maya: Sounds good.
[11:29] Leah: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invite for the benchmark run and share docs.
[11:35] End of call.

POC acceptance criteria (recap):

- Phase 2: synthetic load & tuning (Week 2/3)

Connectivity options summary: VPC Peering / TGW (low latency, cost-efficient at scale) vs PrivateLink (endpoint-based, explicit control & policies) — cost tradeoffs to be included in sizing.
